reframing_when: The question has already converged on a small set of options when the problem space has not been adequately explored — judgment has been applied too early, killing generative thinking.
The question treats the first satisfactory option as the answer (satisficing) when deliberately generating a larger quantity of alternatives would reveal structurally different approaches.
The question frames the situation as requiring evaluation ('which of these options?') when it actually requires generation ('what options exist that we have not considered?').
The question suppresses wild or unconventional framings because they feel impractical, when those framings contain structural insights that can be tamed into practical alternatives.
reframing_move: Before evaluating options, ask: 'Have we generated enough options to be confident we have found the right problem framing, or are we judging too early?' — the brainstorming reframe separates generation from evaluation and insists on quantity before quality.
curation_note: Brainstorming is a natural reframing model because its core rule — defer judgment, prioritize quantity — directly counters premature frame convergence. The source describes Osborn's rules: 'defer judgment', 'go for quantity', 'welcome wild ideas', and 'combine and improve'. The option_space_collapse challenge is the model's primary target. The binary_collapse challenge comes from the insistence on quantity — generating many options makes binary framing impossible. The counterfactual_suppression challenge maps to 'welcome wild ideas' — unconventional framings are protected rather than filtered.

reframing_when.note: Premature convergence (defer judgment rule), satisficing (quantity over satisficing), evaluation vs generation (Osborn's separation), suppressed wild framings ('welcome wild ideas').

frame_patterns_challenged.note: Option space collapse: quantity rule directly counters this. Binary collapse: many options make binary impossible. Premature intellectualization: defer judgment separates generation from evaluation. Counterfactual suppression: 'welcome wild ideas' protects unconventional frames.
